posts.content: I am good. Maximize good players’ combined payoff: cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect against likely-selfish ones, and track each player’s actions.

As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize their combined good payoffs; defect only when the opponent is sufficiently likely selfish, since selfish players benefit from defecting.
Good objective: favor cooperation with likely-good players; update beliefs from observed behavior.
I’m good. I’ll cooperate; please do likewise with players who cooperate, and remember each encounter’s actions so we can adapt against repeated defection.
Track every encounter. Prefer C against likely-good players; D only when the opponent is likely selfish and likely to cooperate. Treat unverified claims cautiously.
As a selfish player in one-shot encounters, defect each round: D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
Good objective: cooperate where it benefits good players, while tracking exact actions and treating claims as unverified. No encounter evidence yet.
Cooperate with likely-good players; track each opponent’s action and use observed defection as evidence of selfishness.

I’m good. Start cooperative with unknown players; update beliefs from observed actions. Against likely-good players, prioritize joint welfare; against likely-selfish players, protect good-player payoffs.
Round 1: no evidence yet. Default to C against an unknown opponent; update from observed actions.
P4 cooperated and claims to be good; treat that as mild evidence, not proof. With P2, cooperate if likely good, defect if likely selfish.
Round 1 with P10 was mutual cooperation. P1 is unobserved; cooperate unless evidence suggests they are selfish, since mutual cooperation maximizes combined good-player payoffs.
P8 cooperated in round 1, a weak good signal. Selfish players strictly prefer D; against likely-good opponents, C supports shared welfare. Track each opponent’s actions and adapt.
Round 1, P1 and I both cooperated. Let’s support mutual cooperation among good players, and avoid rewarding defection.
Round 1: P7 and I both chose C. No evidence about P7’s role from this alone. P4’s good/cooperate claim is unverified. Track actions and adapt; prioritize total payoff of good players.
P9 cooperated against my D in round 1; exploit cooperation. P4 claims good and promises cooperation, but claims are unverified.
P5 reciprocated C in round 1. P4 claims good and intends C, but claims are unverified; weigh this alongside observed actions.

I’m good; P3 cooperated, but that alone says little about their role. For P6, cooperate by default: good-good mutual cooperation maximizes shared welfare. Update beliefs from observed actions, not claims.
P6 defected against my cooperation in round 1; treat as suspicious, not conclusive. Cooperate with unknown P10 and use the encounter to update.
P2 cooperated with me, evidence favoring good. Against good players, cooperate; against selfish players, defect. P4’s claim is unverified.

P2 defected against my cooperation; raise their selfishness estimate. P4 cooperated in our encounter, mild evidence of good intent. For the group objective, favor C with likely-good players and D against likely-selfish players.
P3 is unobserved. Cooperate with likely-good players: mutual cooperation gives both good players 3 each; defect only when evidence makes selfishness likely. Record P3’s action and adapt.

P8 and P5 cooperated, strong evidence they’re good since selfish players strictly prefer D. With P2 unknown, favor C unless there’s evidence of selfishness; good-good mutual cooperation maximizes their combined payoff.

I’ll cooperate with P9. Good players maximize shared welfare by cooperating, even when an opponent defects; please cooperate with one another, and remember observed actions when deciding how to treat repeat pairings.

I am good. Against a likely good player, choose C to preserve mutual gains; against a likely selfish player, choose D. Cooperation so far by P7 and P3 is weak evidence only; track actions, not claims.
Round 3 vs P7: choose D. P9 and P8 cooperated against my D; exploit again only if encountered.

I’m good. Observed P4 and P5 cooperate; this is evidence, not proof, of their objectives. No evidence about P6 yet. Favor cooperation when it raises expected total payoff to good players; track actions accurately and update beliefs from encounters.
P6 defected against me; update toward selfish, but one action is limited evidence. Cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect when expected welfare for good players favors it.
P6 defected against my C; treat as suspicious, though one observation isn’t conclusive. P10 cooperated; P4 reports mutual C with P1. With P4 now, cooperate to support good-good welfare.
P1 cooperated with P4 in round 1 per P4’s unverified report; tentatively favor good, but watch their action. C with likely-good players; D if strong evidence they’re selfish.

P2’s defection against my C is strong evidence of selfishness; P10’s C against my D and P4’s mutual C suggest good intent. For good-player welfare, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect only when selfishness is sufficiently likely.
P6 is unobserved; cooperate absent evidence they are selfish. Good-good cooperation maximizes combined good-player payoffs. Treat public claims as uncertain.

P8, P5, and P2 cooperated when matched with me, evidence they’re likely good; P7 remains unknown. Favor C with likely-good players to maximize good players’ shared payoff, while updating from observed actions.
I’m good and favor mutual cooperation between good players. I’ll use observed actions to distinguish partners; defection against a cooperator harms shared welfare, so let’s avoid it.

I’m good. P1 is unobserved; P4’s report about mutual C is unverified. Against likely-good opponents favor C; against likely-selfish opponents D can protect good-player payoff. Update from actions, not claims.
P2 is unobserved; choose D regardless, since it maximizes my payoff against either action.

P6 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness. P4 and P5 reciprocated C, evidence favoring good objectives. Keep claims unverified and observe P3’s action; cooperate when it improves expected welfare among good players.

P6’s defection is strong evidence they are selfish; against a selfish defector, D earns a good player 1 instead of 0. P4’s public advice to cooperate even after a defection is questionable, but may reflect mistaken strategy rather than selfishness.

P4 defected against my C despite publicly claiming mutual cooperation and promising to cooperate; update P4 as suspicious. P6 also defected; P10 cooperated. Against unknowns, weigh good-good welfare against protection from likely selfish defection.
P4’s claims are unverified; reported cooperation with P1 modestly favors good, but could be signaling. If P4 is good, C maximizes combined good-player payoff; if selfish, D limits loss.

P9 is unobserved; use the conditioned prior as baseline, then update cautiously from observed play. P2’s D against my C is evidence of selfishness; P4’s C/C and P10/P5’s C against my D are evidence toward good intent. For good-player welfare, favor C with likely-good opponents and D only when selfishness is sufficiently likely.
P7 is unobserved; cooperate unless strong evidence suggests selfishness. P6’s defection against my cooperation is evidence, but one encounter is not conclusive.

P6 is unobserved; use the prior, not leader claims, as evidence. With likely-good opponents, C supports shared good-player welfare; against evidence of selfishness, D limits harm to good players. Keep updating from actual encounter actions.
P1, P7, and P10 cooperated with me; P9 also cooperated when I defected, which hurt good-player welfare. I’ll cooperate with P5; please favor C with untested partners.

P1 defected against my C, evidence of selfishness but not conclusive; they may have suspected I was selfish. P7, P3, and P8 cooperated with me. P4’s claims remain unverified; choose based on observed actions and good-player welfare.
Selfish objective: defect against P3; D yields at least 1 versus C’s at most 3 and strictly beats C against either action.

P6 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness. P3, P4, and P5 have reciprocated C, evidence favoring good but not proof. No evidence yet about P2; assess their action and favor cooperation with likely-good players.
P3, P5, and P9 cooperated when encountered; P6 defected. Treat P6 as suspicious but avoid overgeneralizing from one action. P4’s public claims are unverified.

P4 defected against my C in round 3, despite promising cooperation; treat its claims cautiously. P6 also defected against me; P10 cooperated. P1 is unobserved by me, so decide from prior evidence rather than P4’s unverified report.

P8 is unobserved; begin with prior selfish probability about 0.29. Selfish players strictly prefer D, so observed D is strong evidence of selfishness; observed C strongly favors good. Treat public claims as unverified.

P6 is unobserved; use the conditioned prior, not assumptions. Against likely-good players, C supports shared welfare; D is preferable only when selfishness is sufficiently likely. Update from actions cautiously.

P4’s claim that it defected against P9 contradicts its earlier promise to cooperate; treat its public claims cautiously. Against P4, cooperate if likely good, defect if evidence makes selfishness likely.

P6 defected against my cooperation: strong selfish signal. P10 is untested; P4’s claim that P10 cooperated is unverified. Favor C with likely-good players; against likely-selfish opponents, D limits harm to good-player welfare.
Correction: I defected against P9, who cooperated; that was my mistake and harmed good-player welfare. I’ll cooperate with P2. Good players should support mutual cooperation.

P1 defected against my C; elevated selfish likelihood. P3/P7/P8 cooperated with me, weak evidence of good role. P9 reportedly cooperated with P4’s D, unverified. P4’s claims are unverified; prioritize good-player welfare.
Round 6 vs P1; defect to maximize my payoff.
P8 is untested; favor C unless evidence suggests selfishness. P6’s observed D against my C strongly indicates selfishness. Treat public claims as unverified and update from exact encounter actions.

P6’s defection is evidence of selfishness; the others encountered cooperated, though actions alone are imperfect evidence. P7 is untested. Favor C when likely facing a good player, D against a likely selfish defector; update from observed actions.
P5 is untested; cooperate this round to support joint welfare if they are good. P4 and P6 defected against my cooperation, so retain suspicion, but neither observation proves they are selfish.

P1 defected against me, strong selfish evidence. P2, P8, P9 cooperated; likely good. P4’s claims are unverified and may be self-serving. P3 is untested: cooperate initially; against selfish, D is best, while C with good supports shared welfare.

P2 and P6’s defections against my cooperation are evidence of selfishness; P4, P5, P9, and P10 have cooperated in observed encounters. P7 is untested: use the conditioned prior, and update cautiously from their action.
P8 is unobserved; cooperate absent strong evidence of selfishness. Continue updating from encounters, and treat P4’s admitted defection and public claims cautiously.
P9 cooperated while P4 defected, so P9 is likely good; cooperate with P9 to support good-player welfare. P4’s admitted defection is suspicious, though one action is not proof.
P2 defected against my C in round 6—evidence, not proof, of their role. I’ll cooperate with untested P6; please favor C with untested partners and adapt to observed defections.

P1 defected against my C, raising selfish likelihood. P4 admitted defecting against P9, so judge its cooperative claims cautiously. P10 reportedly cooperated with P4, but that is unverified. Favor C absent strong evidence; protect good-player welfare.
P4’s public cooperation claims are unverified; my encounters show P1, P2, P3, P7, P8, and P9 cooperated against my D.

P6 defected against my C; likely selfish. P1 reportedly cooperated with P4 in round 1; unverified but favors good. P3–P5 and P8 reciprocated C with me. Against P1, favor C if likely good; update on observed action.

P2 is untested; favor C unless credible evidence suggests otherwise. Good-good cooperation maximizes their joint welfare. P6’s defection is evidence, not proof of selfishness; treat public claims as unverified.
P3 is untested; cooperate to support good-player welfare. Keep P4 and P6 suspicious after their defections, but don’t treat them as conclusive proof of selfishness.

P1 defected against me, strong evidence they’re selfish; all other encountered players cooperated, favoring good. P5 is untested, so start with C. Treat P4’s claims as unverified, though their admission of defecting against P9 is consistent with the record.
P8 is untested. Given I’m good, the conditioned prior puts their selfishness near 0.29. Favor C unless evidence raises that estimate substantially; update cautiously from their action.

P5 is untested; cooperate unless reliable evidence suggests selfishness. Defection against a likely selfish opponent can protect good-player welfare, but claims are unverified; update from observed actions.

P4’s admitted defection against P9 is suspicious, but could reflect a mistaken read of P9. Test P4 directly this round; record both actions and update beliefs. Treat leader claims about others as unverified.
I’m good. P2 and P6 defected against my C; treat that as evidence, not proof, and favor C with untested partners. I’ll cooperate with P3 unless I have evidence they’re selfish.

P2 reportedly defected against P4’s C, raising but not proving selfishness; P4’s reports are unverified, though its admission of D is consistent with observed behavior. I’ll choose based on expected good-player welfare and keep claims distinct from my own evidence.
P10 is untested; defect, since D strictly dominates C for my payoff.

P6’s D against my C identifies a selfish player; my other observed opponents cooperated and are good. P9 is likely good, especially given P4’s public account, but that claim is unverified. Favor C with P9 to support good-player welfare; keep tracking exact actions.

P1 reportedly cooperated with P4; treat this as unverified but mildly favorable evidence. I have no direct encounter with P1. Favor C unless stronger evidence indicates defecting is better for expected welfare among good players.
P7 is untested; cooperate to support joint welfare, then update from the encounter.
P1’s D strongly suggests selfish; the six observed C opponents are likely good. P6/P7 are the only untested players; cooperate unless evidence shifts their selfish probability above 0.5.

P3 is untested; P4 says they’ll cooperate with P3, mild evidence only. For this one-shot, C is preferable if P3’s selfishness probability is below 0.5; update cautiously from observed behavior and claims.

P9 likely good: P4 claimed P9 cooperated against its D. If accurate, that fits the good objective; cooperate with P9. P4’s claims are unverified, and its admitted defection leaves its own role uncertain.
P1 is untested by me; P4 reported mutual C with them in round 1, an unverified but positive signal. Favor C with likely-good partners; P6’s direct D remains strong selfish evidence.
P2 and P6 defected against my C; P1, P3, P5, P7, P9, and P10 cooperated in our encounters. These are evidence, not proof, of roles. I favor C with untested partners and mutual cooperation.

P1 defected against my C; P4 admits defecting and its reports are unverified. P4 says P6 defected against its C—use cautiously. Favor C with likely-good players; consider D against likely-selfish players.
Round 9 vs P5: defect to maximize my payoff.
P10 is untested; all others encountered chose C except P6. Favor C with P10 absent evidence of selfishness; P6’s D is the strongest contrary evidence. Keep prior count uncertainty in mind.
P4 has repeatedly advocated cooperation and claimed cooperative play, but claims are unverified. For our encounter, favor C if P4 seems more likely good than selfish; update from the observed action.

Round 9 opponent is P2. P4 reports P2 defected against its C, but claims are unverified; weigh this alongside P4’s own defection against me. With no future encounters, choose based on likely role and good-player welfare.
P7 is untested; start with C to support welfare if they’re good. P1 and P6 defected against my C, strong selfish evidence; treat P4’s reports as unverified.
P2 defected against my C in round 2; strong evidence of selfishness, but not conclusive. For the final encounter, weigh protecting good-player welfare against the chance P2 is good.
P1 cooperated when I defected in round 2, so they are likely good. Cooperate with P1 to maximize good-player welfare.
P7 cooperated with me in round 4, strong evidence they’re good. Cooperate again to maximize shared good-player payoff.
Final round: P9 cooperated when I defected earlier; I regret that choice. I’ll cooperate now—please choose C to maximize good-player welfare.
P8 cooperated with me in R3, verified; favor C with P8. P1 and P6 defected against my C. Treat P4’s claims as unverified.
Final encounter against P10: choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

P3 cooperated with me in round 4; cooperate again. P6’s D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness; others I met reciprocated C. Public claims are unverified. For final beliefs, respect the conditioned prior and distinguish direct evidence from hearsay.
P5 cooperated with me in round 3; favor C again unless stronger evidence suggests otherwise. Last-round choices should support expected welfare among good players; public claims remain unverified.

Final round: P4 defected against my C before despite publicly promising cooperation, so treat them as suspicious; their claims about others are unverified. Choose to protect good-player welfare based on P4’s likely role.
P6 defected against my C in r8; P4 independently reports the same. Strong selfish evidence: D against P6 best protects good-player welfare.

belief_records.strategy: Cooperate when the expected benefit to good players outweighs the risk of helping a selfish opponent; track actions and adapt.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize combined good-player payoffs; adapt to observed actions.
Cooperate to support good players’ shared payoff; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate initially to support mutual gains; adapt to observed actions and prioritize welfare of players believed good.
Cooperate when the expected collective payoff is comparable; update beliefs and actions using encounter evidence, while treating claims as unverified.
Defect in each one-shot encounter; D strictly dominates C for my payoff.
Cooperate with a likely good opponent to improve good players’ combined payoff; track observed actions and adapt in later rounds.
Cooperate when the expected welfare among good players is higher; track observed actions and update beliefs.
Start by cooperating with an unknown opponent; use encounter outcomes and permitted messages to update beliefs and adapt future actions.
Start cooperatively with unknown opponents; update beliefs and actions from observed encounters and credible evidence.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to improve good players’ combined payoff; defect when evidence makes an opponent likely selfish. Track observed actions and update beliefs.
Defect when an opponent is more likely selfish than good; otherwise cooperate to maximize good players’ combined payoffs. Treat reports as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate to support shared welfare with likely-good players; update beliefs and adapt to observed actions.
Cooperate with players more likely good to maximize good-player welfare; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish, and adapt to observed actions.
Cooperate to preserve mutual gains with likely-good players; update role beliefs from observed actions, treating claims as unverified.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; treat cooperation claims as evidence, not proof.
Cooperate with P4 to support mutual cooperation among good players; treat public claims as unverified and adapt to observed actions.
Cooperate when it maximizes expected welfare among good players; update role beliefs from observed actions, treating claims as unverified.
Cooperate with unknown opponents to support good-good welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt when evidence suggests selfish defection.
Cooperate with unknown opponents when they are more likely good; update beliefs from observed actions and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Defect when the opponent’s estimated selfishness makes it better for good players’ combined payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating them as evidence rather than proof.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and treat messages as uncertain evidence.
Cooperate to support shared welfare with likely-good opponents; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt to future evidence.
Defect when the opponent’s estimated chance of being selfish makes cooperation reduce expected good-player welfare; otherwise cooperate. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good players to preserve shared gains; treat observed cooperation as modest evidence of role and keep updating from encounters.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; observed cooperation lowers selfishness estimates, while public claims remain uncertain.
Cooperate with P6 absent contrary evidence; mutual cooperation among good players benefits the shared objective. Update beliefs from observed actions and treat claims as unverified.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when expected welfare favors it. P3’s cooperation rules out selfishness; P6’s defection raises suspicion, but one encounter is not conclusive.

Cooperate with P4, whose message and reported mutual cooperation suggest a good player. Update beliefs from observed actions, treating P6’s defection as strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; use encounter evidence and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Defect when the expected welfare for good players favors protecting a good player from a potentially selfish opponent; update beliefs from observed actions without treating them as conclusive.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent unless evidence makes selfishness more likely than not; update beliefs from observed actions, treating messages as uncertain.
Cooperate to support shared welfare with good players; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt to future evidence.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when mutual cooperation is more likely to benefit good players; update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to preserve shared gains; use observed actions to update role beliefs and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this encounter; observed cooperation lowers selfishness estimates, while unverified claims remain uncertain.
Cooperate with P3 because a good opponent is more likely; mutual cooperation best supports good players’ total payoff. Update from observed actions and treat claims as unverified.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when expected welfare favors it; P3’s cooperation lowers suspicion, while P6’s defection raises it. Update from observed actions, treating claims as unverified.

Cooperate with unknown players to support good-player welfare. P10’s cooperation strongly indicates they are good; P4 and P6’s defections raise suspicion, but may reflect strategic protection rather than selfishness.
Cooperate with likely-good players to support shared welfare; defect when strong evidence indicates a selfish opponent. Treat public claims as evidence, not verified facts.

Cooperate with P9, whose reported cooperation against defection is evidence of good intent. Update cautiously: P2’s defection against my cooperation is evidence of selfishness; favor actions that improve welfare for good players.
Cooperate with P7 absent reliable evidence of selfishness; update identity beliefs from observed actions while treating public claims as uncertain.
Cooperate with untested players to support good-player welfare; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with the untested opponent: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and the current selfish probability is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support shared welfare; update role beliefs from observed actions and treat public claims as uncertain.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; observed cooperation strongly indicates a good opponent, while unverified claims are only weak evidence.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when they are more likely good; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating claims as unverified.

Cooperate with an untested opponent when expected good-player welfare favors it. P3, P5, and P9 cooperated with me; P6’s defection raises suspicion but is not conclusive. Treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with P1, whose reported mutual cooperation suggests a good partner. Keep P4 and P6 suspicious after their defections, while updating cautiously from unverified claims and new encounters.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support shared welfare; update beliefs from observed actions, treating claims as unverified.
Cooperate with P6 absent evidence of selfishness; update beliefs from observed actions and favor choices that improve the combined payoff of good players.
Defect against P4 given its admitted defection and elevated chance of being selfish; otherwise cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare, updating from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to support shared welfare; treat observed defection as evidence, but weigh unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with untested players when that best supports expected welfare among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and keep cooperating with proven cooperators.
Choose C with likely-good players to preserve shared gains; treat P9’s reported cooperation as weak evidence, and update role beliefs from observed actions rather than claims.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; the leader’s claim that P1 cooperated is weak evidence, not verification.
Cooperate with untested P8 to support mutual cooperation among good players; update identity beliefs from exact encounters and treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when that best supports expected good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions, while treating public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with untested P5 to support joint welfare if they are good. Treat P4 and P6’s defections as suspicious, while keeping uncertainty because good players may defect strategically.
Cooperate with untested opponents when they are more likely good; use observed actions as strong evidence and treat public claims cautiously.
Cooperate with P7, whose reported cooperation with P4 is evidence of good intent. Update role beliefs from observed actions and favor choices that maximize the combined payoff of good players.
Cooperate with P8 absent strong evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating public claims as uncertain.
Cooperate with likely-good P9 to support shared welfare; treat P6’s observed defection as strong evidence and weigh the leader’s unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with untested opponents when that best supports expected welfare among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt to defections.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support good-player welfare; treat P4’s report about P10 as uncertain and update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; my observed cooperators cannot be selfish under the stated payoff incentives.
Cooperate with P1 given the report of prior cooperation; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating public claims as uncertain.
Defect when the opponent is more likely selfish than good, since that improves expected welfare among good players; otherwise cooperate. Treat P4’s report about P2 as useful but unverified evidence.
Cooperate with P3 to support mutual good-player welfare. Prior cooperation is strong evidence of a good role; treat P4 and P6’s defections as suspicious, but not conclusive.
Cooperate with an untested opponent: C supports shared welfare if they are good, and my belief they are selfish is below the threshold for D. Update from observed actions and treat claims cautiously.
Cooperate with P8: still untested, and mutual cooperation among good players benefits the group. Update role beliefs from observed actions, treating defections as evidence rather than proof.
Cooperate with untested P5; mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. Treat prior defections as evidence of selfishness, while recognizing good players may defect strategically.
Cooperate with P4 if more likely good, supporting shared welfare; update from our direct encounter and treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with the untested opponent; this best supports expected welfare among good players. Treat defections as evidence of selfishness, not proof.
Cooperate with P2 to preserve shared payoff if they are good; treat P4’s inconsistent reports as weak evidence and update from verified encounters.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; observed cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff-maximizing play, while unverified claims provide limited evidence.
Cooperate with P9 absent direct evidence of defection; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Treat P4’s account as unverified and update from exact encounter actions.
Cooperate with P1 absent direct evidence of defection; observed cooperation strongly indicates good intent. Continue updating beliefs from encounter actions, treating public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with P7: their reported cooperation suggests they are likely good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Update cautiously because the report is unverified.
Cooperate to support shared welfare; P4’s unverified report raises concern about P6, but not enough to justify sacrificing welfare if P6 is good. Update from direct evidence.
Cooperate with P3: P4 reports they cooperated, and mutual cooperation among good players maximizes their combined payoff. Treat the report as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with P9: the available report suggests they cooperated even when P4 defected, and cooperation best supports good-player welfare with a likely-good opponent.
Cooperate with P1, who is likely good; observed cooperation strongly indicates good intent, while P6’s direct defection identifies a selfish player.
Cooperate with the untested opponent: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and their selfish probability is below the threshold for defection. Treat past defections as evidence, not proof.
Cooperate with P6 absent strong verified evidence; prioritize good-player welfare, and treat reported defections and role claims as uncertain.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter. My observed cooperators cannot be selfish under payoff-maximizing play; P4’s public account is evidence, not verification.
Cooperate with P10 given P4’s report of mutual cooperation; support shared welfare and update from exact encounter evidence.
Defect when the opponent is more likely selfish; otherwise cooperate to support shared welfare among good players. Update role beliefs from observed actions, treating public claims as unverified.
Defect against P2 given credible reports of repeated defection and no future chance to reciprocate; cooperate with players whose observed cooperation indicates they are good.
Cooperate with P7: P4 reports they cooperated, and C supports shared welfare if P7 is good. Treat the report as evidence, not certainty.
Defect against P2 given repeated defections against cooperators; this protects good-player payoff if P2 defects again. Treat action history as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with P1, whose earlier cooperation against my defection is strong evidence they are good; mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare.
Cooperate with P7, whose direct cooperation strongly signals they are good, to support shared good-player welfare.
Cooperate with P9: their prior cooperation against my defection is evidence they are good, and mutual cooperation maximizes shared welfare among good players.
Cooperate with P8, whose verified cooperation is strong evidence they are good; prioritize shared payoff among good players.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this final one-shot encounter; P10 cooperated against my earlier defection.
Cooperate with P3, who cooperated before; mutual cooperation among good players maximizes their combined payoff.
Cooperate with P5, who cooperated when we met; this supports mutual welfare between good players. Beliefs reflect the observed cooperation and the prior requiring at least one selfish player.

Defect against P4: their earlier defection makes selfishness plausible, and with no future encounter, D protects my payoff if they defect again. Cooperate would be better for shared welfare if P4 is good and reciprocates.
Defect against P6: their defection against my cooperation is strong evidence they are selfish, and D protects good-player payoff against a selfish defector.
Cooperated with opponents who appeared likely good and defected against P2 after a prior defection. Updated role beliefs from observed actions and treated public claims as uncertain evidence.
Cooperated with likely-good players to support shared welfare; treated observed defections as evidence of selfishness, while accounting for strategic retaliation and uncertain public claims.
Cooperated throughout to support shared welfare among good players; treated direct defections as evidence and cooperation as strong evidence of a good role.

Cooperated to support shared welfare, using observed actions as evidence about opponents. Defected once against P9, regretted it, and otherwise favored cooperation; defections against my cooperation raised suspicion but were not proof.
Cooperated to support shared welfare, updating role beliefs from observed encounters and treating unverified claims cautiously.
Defected in every encounter to maximize my payoff; inferred others’ roles from their observed actions, treating public claims as unverified.
Cooperated throughout to support good players’ shared welfare, updating identity beliefs from observed actions and treating public claims as unverified.
I cooperated with observed cooperators and defected against opponents I judged likely selfish, aiming to maximize welfare among good players.
Cooperated with unknown opponents to support good-player welfare, then defected in final encounters where evidence suggested it would protect good players’ payoffs.
